subject: english-language
topicDisplay: Paper 1: Explorations in Creative Reading and Writing
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: Section A: Reading — one literature fiction text
Section B: Writing — descriptive or narrative writing

questions.q: What type of text do students read in Section A of Paper 1?
questions.explain: Section A of Paper 1 is based on a single unseen literature fiction text from the 20th or 21st century.

questions.q: What kind of writing does Section B of Paper 1 require?
questions.explain: Section B asks students to produce their own descriptive or narrative writing, usually in response to a choice of two tasks.

questions.q: How long is the AQA GCSE English Language Paper 1?
questions.explain: Paper 1 lasts 1 hour 45 minutes and is worth 50% of the GCSE.

questions.q: How many questions are there in Section A (Reading) of Paper 1?
questions.explain: Section A contains four reading questions of increasing demand and mark value.

questions.q: What is the total mark for Paper 1?
questions.explain: Paper 1 is worth 80 marks in total, split equally between Section A (Reading) and Section B (Writing).

questions.q: Which assessment objective covers identifying and interpreting explicit and implicit information and ideas?
questions.explain: AO1 requires students to identify and interpret explicit and implicit information and ideas.

questions.q: Which assessment objective requires students to evaluate texts critically and support their views with textual references?
questions.explain: AO4 is about evaluating texts critically and supporting the response with appropriate textual references.

questions.q: How many assessment objectives are set out in the AQA GCSE English Language specification?
questions.explain: The specification lists six assessment objectives, AO1 to AO6, distributed across the two papers.

questions.q: Which assessment objective is NOT assessed anywhere in Paper 1?
questions.explain: AO3 (comparing writers' ideas and perspectives across texts) is assessed in Paper 2, not Paper 1.

questions.q: The final 20-mark reading question asks students to respond critically to a statement about the text. Which AO does it assess?
questions.explain: The 20-mark evaluation question assesses AO4, requiring critical evaluation supported by textual references.

questions.q: A reading question asking 'How does the writer use language to...?' primarily assesses which AO?
questions.explain: Analysing how writers use language to achieve effects, using subject terminology, is AO2.

questions.q: A question asking how the writer has structured the whole text to interest the reader assesses which AO?
questions.explain: AO2 covers both language and structure, so the whole-text structure question is an AO2 task.

questions.q: In Section B, which AO rewards accurate spelling, punctuation and a range of sentence structures?
questions.explain: AO6 assesses technical accuracy, including vocabulary range, sentence structures, spelling and punctuation.

questions.q: Which AO rewards communicating clearly and imaginatively and organising ideas coherently in the writing task?
questions.explain: AO5 covers clear, effective and imaginative communication and the organisation of information and ideas.

questions.q: What proportion of the marks for the whole GCSE must be awarded for technical accuracy (AO6)?
questions.explain: AO6 (technical accuracy) accounts for 20% of the marks across the specification as a whole.

questions.q: The first reading question, asking students to list four things about a character or setting, mainly assesses which AO?
questions.explain: Listing explicit information from the text is a straightforward AO1 task.

questions.q: A student writes: 'The verb "crept" and the personification of the fog create a sense of menace.' Which reading skill is being demonstrated?
questions.explain: Naming techniques and explaining their effect uses relevant subject terminology, which is AO2.

questions.q: A task reads: 'Write a description suggested by the picture of a storm at sea.' Which section and marks does this belong to?
options: Section B, assessing AO5 and AO6
Section A, assessing AO1 and AO2
Section B, assessing AO2 and AO4
questions.explain: A description task is Section B writing, marked for AO5 (content and organisation) and AO6 (technical accuracy).

questions.q: A question gives the statement 'The writer makes this part of the text tense and dramatic' and asks how far you agree, using the text. Which question type is this?
questions.explain: Responding critically to a given statement about a section of the text is the AO4 evaluation question.

questions.q: A student is deciding between 'Describe a busy market' and 'Write a story about an unexpected visitor.' What are they choosing between?
options: A descriptive task and a narrative task in Section B
Two different reading questions in Section A
An AO2 and an AO4 reading task
A Paper 1 and a Paper 2 task
questions.explain: Section B offers a choice between descriptive and narrative writing, and students answer only one.

specSource: AQA GCSE English Language (8700) specification; Paper 1: Explorations in Creative Reading and Writing
